title: Operating system responsibilities
content: An operating system manages processes, memory, files, devices, permissions, and interfaces between applications and hardware. Processes have isolated address spaces and resources; the OS schedules work and mediates access.

title: CPU and memory overview
content: The CPU executes instructions and coordinates computation. RAM holds active data and code temporarily; storage retains data across power loss. Cache is smaller, faster memory near the processor that reduces access latency. These are different roles and capacities.

title: Networking fundamentals
content: IP addresses identify network interfaces for routing. DNS maps domain names to records such as IP addresses. TCP provides an ordered reliable byte stream; UDP sends datagrams without TCP's delivery guarantees. Routers forward packets between networks.

title: Database concepts
content: Relational databases organize records in tables. Primary keys uniquely identify rows; foreign keys connect tables. SQL retrieves and changes data. Transactions group operations so they commit consistently or roll back. Constraints help protect data integrity.

title: Security fundamentals
content: Authentication checks identity; authorization determines permitted actions. Use least privilege, secure password storage with purpose-built hashing, validated inputs, updates, and backups. Encryption protects confidentiality in transit or at rest, depending on implementation.
cautions: Never store API secrets in source code or expose private credentials in logs.

title: Software architecture layers
content: Layered designs separate responsibilities such as user interface, application orchestration, domain logic, and persistence/infrastructure. Depend on stable interfaces and keep domain logic testable without external services.

title: Local versus cloud computing
content: Local computing runs on the user's hardware, offering direct control and often offline availability but limited local resources. Cloud services run on remote infrastructure and can scale, but require network access and careful privacy, cost, and reliability management.

title: Files, paths, and environments
content: A filesystem path identifies a location; absolute paths start from a root, relative paths depend on the current working directory. Virtual environments isolate Python dependencies. Record versions and use reproducible setup steps to avoid environment confusion.
